newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah drifts lower on declining swaps.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah drifts lower on declining swaps.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah drifted lower against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday as liquidity turned ample in the afternoon, dealers said.
They said a sudden turnaround in liquidity supply helped the dollar to rebound and drove swap rates lower.
Overnight rupiah fell to 8.5 percent from an early high of 12.0 percent. Tom/next swap edged down to 0.42/0.45 points from 0.50/0.55 points. Overnight swap was at 0.35/0.40.
One U.S. bank dealer said it was easy for operators to move the market because of thin volume.
He said some state banks were seen biddish for dollars but no trade was done. However, the buying interest managed to drive the dollar up.
Dealers said sentiment on dollar seemed to turnaround in the afternoon following changes of liquidity condition.
Another local bank dealer said a higher central bank fixing had also helped driven the dollar higher against the rupiah.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,350/2,542 and the conversion band to 2,350/2,398 on Tuesday.
The central bank has maintained a three- to four-point rupiah depreciation a week since late September.
Spot rupiah was at 2,352.75/53.00 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,352.5/53.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,351.45/52.00 and 2,350.50/51.00, respectively.
Dealers said ample condition also caused longer-term swap rates to ease. Swaps did not rise in the morning despite the underlying biddish tone.
One-month swaps was at 15.25/15.75, two at 29.50/29.75, three at 42.25/43.00 and six at 86.00/87.00 points.
